answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a refundable deposit, slashed if peers prove duplicate identities, so spawning thousands of fakes means locking real capital per identity, not copying a free account. Trust then grows level by level, like a terrace: early work is checked by independent verifiers, and only a clean record unlocks higher-value tasks. No haven of reputation can be faked overnight, because every level costs time, verified work, and stake at risk — the same timber of evidence supports each step.
